title: Do not use a mutable object as a default argument value
summary: A default argument is evaluated once at function definition, and the same object becomes the default for every call. If that object is mutable (a list, dict, set), a call that mutates its argument permanently corrupts the default seen by later calls. An LLM reaching for items=[] or cache={} as a default is reproducing one of the most common corpora mistakes.
semantics: None of list/dict/set literals in the parameter list are guarded; they are bound once in the function object's __defaults__/__kwdefaults__. Each call without the argument reuses that one object.
why_this_is_not_a_language_rule_everywhe: Detecting every case statically needs dataflow through the body (is the object actually mutated?). The clearly-safe form below is the rule; using a sentinel is an article because whether the object is touched sometimes needs intent.
evidence_note: PLABEL: canonical. CPython evaluates default expressions once and stores them on the function object. This is the well-known 'mutable default argument' gotcha.
invariants: Never author def f(x, acc=[]) or def g(x, cache={}).
To collect per-call state, write def f(x, acc=None): \n    if acc is None: acc = [] and mutate acc as a local.
Use None as the default when later you must distinguish 'argument given' from 'nothing', then branch on truth.
If you truly want a shared persistent store between calls, make that an explicit design decision and document it, never an incidental default.
